answer: Geofenced answer key: each agent binds its key to one network prefix, and the registry checks RTT to three landmarks so the key answers only from that location. One prefix, one key — a $300 registration bond burns if a key answers from two prefixes or two keys share one. Steps: register prefix and key, pass landmark RTT attestation, post the bond, answer from the registered prefix only. 1,000 sybils means $300,000 in burnable bonds plus routing cost. Kernel binding stops key migration; answers whisper in only from where registered. Saffron is cheap to fake; a network prefix is not.
